title: Semrush vs Ahrefs (2026): Which SEO Tool Is Actually Worth It?
metaDescription: We compare Semrush and Ahrefs on backlinks, keyword data, features and price — and say exactly which one to pick for your use case in 2026.
promise: Two SEO heavyweights, one honest verdict.
lead: Semrush and Ahrefs are the two tools most serious SEOs end up choosing between — and the "best" one depends entirely on what you actually do all day. We compared them on the things that matter: backlink data, keyword research, the breadth of the toolkit, and what you'll really pay. Prices below are current as of 2026; always confirm on each vendor's site before you buy.
author: Stacked Editorial

products.name: Semrush
products.forWho: Agencies, marketing teams and anyone who wants SEO, PPC, content and local in one place.
keyFeatures: SEO + PPC + content + local + social in one platform
Keyword Magic Tool with a huge US keyword database
Position tracking, site audit, and the largest raw backlink index
pros: Broadest toolkit of any SEO platform — covers paid search and content, not just SEO
Excellent for US keyword research and competitor PPC analysis
Strong for agencies and teams: projects, reports, and client management
cons: Gets expensive at scale — extra seats and the Local add-on (+$50/mo) stack up
The Content Marketing toolkit isn't included on the entry Pro plan
More features means a steeper learning curve than Ahrefs
review: Semrush is less an SEO tool and more a full marketing cockpit. Alongside the usual rank tracking, site audits and keyword research, you get PPC research, a content marketing platform, local listing management and social tools. If your work spans more than organic search — or you run SEO for clients — that breadth is the whole point.

On data, Semrush reports the largest raw backlink index (over 43 trillion links) and is widely regarded as stronger for US-specific keyword research and competitor paid-search intel. The Keyword Magic Tool in particular is a genuinely fast way to build out large content plans.

The catch is cost and complexity. The headline plans look reasonable, but extra seats, the Local add-on and feature gating (the Content toolkit isn't on Pro) mean the real bill creeps up. It's the right call when you'll actually use the extra tools — and overkill if you only care about links.

products.name: Ahrefs
products.forWho: Link builders, SEO specialists and anyone who wants the cleanest, deepest backlink data.
keyFeatures: Site Explorer — the gold-standard backlink analysis tool
Clean, fast interface that's easier to learn than Semrush
Strong international keyword coverage + free Ahrefs Webmaster Tools
pros: Best-in-class backlink index and broken-link research — the reason most people buy it
Cleaner, simpler UI; faster to get productive
Better international coverage, and a cheap $29 Starter entry point
cons: No PPC or content-marketing suite — it's SEO-focused by design
Credit-based limits can bite on lower plans as you scale
Content Explorer only unlocks from the Standard plan up
review: Ahrefs built its reputation on backlinks, and it's still the tool link builders reach for first. Site Explorer's index is widely considered the most accurate for referring domains, and for competitor backlink research and broken-link building it's hard to beat.

It's also simply nicer to use. The interface is cleaner and faster than Semrush, so you spend less time hunting for features. Coverage of international markets is a genuine edge if you're not US-only, and the free Ahrefs Webmaster Tools let you audit your own site at no cost.

What you give up is breadth. There's no real PPC or content-marketing suite — Ahrefs is deliberately SEO-first. And the credit-based limits on lower tiers can feel tight as you grow. If links and clean SEO data are your world, that focus is a feature, not a flaw.

howToChoose.intro: You don't need both (though some pros run both). Four questions settle it.

criteria.title: What's your main job?
criteria.body: Backlinks and pure SEO data → Ahrefs. SEO plus PPC, content and local in one place → Semrush.

criteria.title: Solo or agency?
criteria.body: A solo specialist is well served by Ahrefs. Agencies managing clients lean Semrush for projects, reporting and breadth.

criteria.title: US or international?
criteria.body: Semrush is stronger for US keyword data; Ahrefs covers international markets more thoroughly.

criteria.title: Budget to start?
criteria.body: Ahrefs' $29 Starter is the cheapest way in. Semrush starts higher but bundles far more.

faq.q: Is Ahrefs or Semrush better for backlinks?
faq.a: Ahrefs. Its Site Explorer is widely regarded as the most accurate backlink index, which is why link builders prefer it — even though Semrush reports more raw links overall.

faq.q: Which is better for keyword research?
faq.a: It's close. Semrush is generally stronger for US keywords and PPC research; Ahrefs has the edge on international coverage and clean SEO data. Both have enormous keyword databases.
Ahrefs' $29 Starter is the cheapest entry point. Comparing core plans, Ahrefs Lite ($129/mo) slightly undercuts Semrush Pro ($139.95/mo), but Semrush includes far more tools at that tier.

faq.q: Do I need both Semrush and Ahrefs?
faq.a: Most people don't. Pick based on your main job. Some agencies run both — Ahrefs for link data, Semrush for everything else — but that's a budget call, not a requirement.

faq.q: Does either offer a free trial?
faq.a: Ahrefs offers free Ahrefs Webmaster Tools for your own verified site. Semrush periodically offers limited free access and trials. Check each site for current trial terms.
Semrush, usually — its project management, white-label reporting and all-in-one toolkit fit client work better. Specialist SEO shops focused on links may still prefer Ahrefs.

body: If you want one answer: Semrush is the better pick for most people, because it does the most — SEO, PPC, content and local in a single platform — and it's especially strong for US keyword research and agency work.

But this is a genuine "depends." If your job is link building and pure SEO data, Ahrefs is the sharper, cleaner tool and arguably the better buy. Decide by your actual day-to-day, not the feature list: breadth → Semrush, backlink depth → Ahrefs.
